intro: You asked for *"tags on orders so ops can group them"*. Before I draft the spec I need the decisions below. Each screen shows what I already know, the options I see, and what each one costs. Use the panel on the right to ask me anything; I answer in the next round.

decisions.title: Who is the primary user of order tags?
decisions.why: Mixing audiences optimizes the wrong workflow; permissions and defaults differ per actor.
decisions.context: The repo has an `ops` Django group with a custom admin, and a customer-facing dashboard under `dashboard/`. Nothing in the prompt says which one.

options.label: Internal ops staff
options.description: Tags live in the ops admin only.
options.consequences: No customer-facing UI in v1; permissions reduce to the existing ops group.

options.label: Tenant admins
options.description: Customers tag their own orders in the dashboard.
options.consequences: Per-tenant tag namespaces, dashboard UI, and a public API surface — roughly doubles the plan.

options.label: Both, shared tags
options.description: Ops and tenant admins see the same tags.
options.consequences: Needs a visibility rule per tag (internal vs shared) from day one.

decisions.title: What do they do today without tags?
decisions.why: No current pain means no demand to validate; the workaround tells us the real objective.

input.label: Describe the workaround and its pain
input.placeholder: Ops keeps a spreadsheet of order ids per campaign and re-exports it weekly

decisions.title: Two people edit the same order's tags within seconds. Who wins?
decisions.why: Silent last-write-wins eats user work; the rule has to be explicit in the spec.
decisions.context:
Your journey in A2 has tags edited from the order page **and** from a bulk import. Both can touch the same order.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[Order page] --> O[(Order #4411)]
  B[Bulk import] --> O
  O --> C{Conflict?}
```

options.label: Last write wins
options.description: Simplest. The later save replaces the earlier one.
options.consequences: Silent data loss on overlap. Acceptable only if overlap is genuinely rare.

options.label: Optimistic lock
options.description: The second save sees a conflict and must reload.
options.consequences: Reuses the `last_updated_at` guard the bulk upsert already has. One extra error state in the UI.

options.label: Merge tag sets
options.consequences: Removals become ambiguous (did they remove it, or never see it?). Needs a tombstone design — a new plan phase.
